ex_kr: Sand: the exact curve crosses the dashed line $K_r=\kappa$ at $h_c=199$\,cm (dot). This is \cref{eq:s-hc} with $\alpha=0.145$, $n=2.68$, $\ell=0.5$.
Loam: the crossing is at $h_c=9\,209$\,cm, just below $10^4$\,cm, with $\alpha=0.036$, $n=1.56$.
Sand at field capacity (100\,cm): $K_r=2.5\times10^{-8}$, a fraction of the saturated conductivity that is already tiny; the worked example of Part~2 of the guide.
Dotted lines: the dry-end straight line $m^2(\alpha h)^{-E}$. It lies on the exact curve wherever $\alpha h\gg1$, which is why the closed form of the reach is accurate.
Grey band (300--600\,cm): the usual triggers. They lie beyond the reach of sand and well inside the reach of loam.
The constant $\kappa$: the relative conductivity below which a crop can no longer dry the soil at the sensor within a season; one value for all ten soils.
ex_kappa: The minimum: $\log_{10}\kappa=-9.46$, $\kappa=3.47\times10^{-10}$, loss $L=0.196$\,decades$^2$. At this value 5 soils lie outside their interval: S01 by 0.11 decade, S02 by 0.27 decade, S03 by 0.12 decade, S04 by 0.23 decade, S05 by 0.21 decade; the other 5 lie inside.
Left edge of the bootstrap interval, $\kappa=9.8e-11$: resampling the ten soils with replacement 1\,000 times and refitting.
Right edge, $\kappa=2.8e-09$. The interval spans 1.5 decades, but the reach changes only by a factor 1.45 to 2.45 per decade of $\kappa$.
Too small a $\kappa$ puts every predicted reach too far into the dry range: the soils with a finite interval (sand, loamy sand, sandy loam) are missed and the loss rises.
Too large a $\kappa$ predicts reaches that are too short: soils whose triggers fire up to $10^4$\,cm are missed.
ex_e2: Sand, the driest trigger that still fires: 100\,cm brings 6.36\,mm a year, above the 5\,mm line.
Sand, the next trigger, 150\,cm, brings 0.0\,mm: it never fires. The observed reach lies between the two (green band, 100--150\,cm).
The reach predicted by the closed form, 199\,cm (dashed): a third above the band, the largest miss among the soils with a finite interval.
The 5\,mm a year threshold that defines ``fires; with 1, 10, 20 or 40\,mm the fitted $\kappa$ becomes 2.7, 7.3, 13 or 25 $\times10^{-10}$.
Loam, the driest trigger that fires: 5000\,cm brings 5.16\,mm a year.
Predicted reach of loam, 9\,209\,cm: inside the observed band 5\,000--10\,000\,cm.
Loam at the usual 300\,cm trigger: 212\,mm a year of irrigation, the trigger works.
ex_fate: Soil evaporation: 82.4\,mm more than the rainfed twin; $\eta_{E_s}=0.37$, the largest share in this run because the surface is wetted every few days.
The rest, 10.7\,mm, is the change of storage and runoff, obtained by difference so that the shares add to one.
The whole bar is the irrigation of the run, $I=222.5$\,mm a year: one bar is one irrigated millimetre scaled up.
ex_dose: $d=1$\,mm: $1-e^{-1/3.9}=0.23$; $\eta_D=0.045$. A small dose is used the same day and almost nothing drains.
The plateau $\eta_\infty=0.197$ of loam: the share of a large dose that drains, set by the race between drainage and uptake.
